summary: The author opened a new conversation and asked the model to check access to the repository and pick up handover 12.
verbatim: Please check if you have access to c:\git\business-intelligence and then look for Handover_12 in the handovers folder. Let's take it from there.

summary: Confirmed access (folder granted), read handover 12; reported HEAD 050f467, 9 commits ahead of origin/main, about 100 stale lock files in .git; proposed the first actions and asked for deletion permission for S12.
The author approved going ahead, including deletion permission for the session.

Ran handover 12's first actions: deletion approved for S12; removed the stale-* lock files from .git; tree clean, HEAD 050f467, 9 ahead of origin/main (unpushed); check_repo.py on a cloud copy (git archive) passes with the 3 known S07 warnings (11 sessions, 36 ADRs); read ADR-0032, model/README.md, the named declarations, ADR-0027, ADR-0030, ADR-0031, 149 and ARC-OP-29; sandbox status at 2016-06-02, 11.97 GB free; runner idle, last load 2016-06-02; opened S12.

Queried the sandbox (s12-ties) for versions of one key with equal ValidFrom across current and history tables of the 17 system-versioned tables: 11 ties (People 3, StateProvinces 7, Customers 1), all zero-length versions; checked that DuckDB TIMESTAMP truncates the seventh decimal and TIMESTAMP_NS keeps it; read the manifest fields.

Drafted 143, the vault generator: files and headers, SHA-256 hash keys and key preparation, row metadata with knowledge time as the extract's date, load pattern per kind, ordering, ties and late arrivals, one pattern for the first day and every day, batches, staging, tests, and three choices for the author.

sol reviewed 143 alone against the stated standard and failed it with five findings: a late arrival makes a suppressed later version reconstruct wrongly; a failed partial batch keeps rows a fixed model cannot replace; the audit hashdiff does not separate versions in one instant; tie numbering depends on a per-satellite hashdiff; load=never conflicts with exact reconstruction.

check.expected: a generator buildable from the note without guessing; deterministic, idempotent, append-only loads; exact reconstruction by source version; nothing silently lost or duplicated; no batch visible half-loaded

summary: Applied all five findings to 143: restatement of the next version on a late arrival; failed batches deleted by a pre-hook before retry, published batches never; audit satellite without change detection; source_seq computed once per source row from ValidTo and a whole-row hash; load=never named as the one exception to exact reconstruction; tests added.
Put the revised 143 to the author with its three choices: keep the 11 zero-length versions; start the vault at 2016-05-31 by replaying the three kept extracts; add key_case to the source declaration.

blocker.detail: the author's ruling on 143 and its three choices

summary: The author ruled the three choices of 143 as recommended: keep zero-length versions; start the vault at 2016-05-31 by replaying the kept extracts; add key_case to the source declaration.

Recorded the ruling: ADR-0037; 143 marked RULED; ARC-OP-29 note; key_case added to model/README.md, model/sources/wwi.md, the transcription (reproduces the file byte for byte), model_lib and check_model.

Built the vault generator (generate.py, six SQL templates, scope.txt): staging views, hubs, links, payload, milestone, audit, status-tracking and effectivity satellites and a reference table, with generated tests, for People, Customers, Orders and Colors; --check catches an edited and a stray file.

Wrote and ran the cloud suite on the three kept extracts with the runner's landing code and versions: clean, twice, failed batch, reconstruction (planted defect caught) and constructed late arrival all pass. Two defects found and fixed: ValidTo 9999-12-31 overflows TIMESTAMP_NS (kept as text); the duplicate rule dropped People's 3 zero-length versions (end now part of it; nothing_dropped test added, fails on the old build).

check.expected: three daily loads pass; reloading changes nothing; a failed batch leaves nothing; every delivered version reconstructs; a late arrival is restated
check.observed: all five pass after two fixes; 158,011 versions reconstructed

summary: Recorded in 143 section 13 what changed while building (effectivity as one row per change, the period end as text, the duplicate rule, the generator's scope); wrote the generated models into the live dbt project, replacing the smoke model.

Set the old warehouse aside (data/warehouse_pre-vault_2026-11-04), committed the generated project (542dedb); the runner replayed 2016-05-31 to 06-02, all three loads ok with 123 tests passing, published; the 35 vault tables match the cloud clean load row for row (content fingerprints identical).

check.expected: the runner's load on the author's machine equals the cloud suite's clean load
check.observed: 35 of 35 tables identical in count and content fingerprint

summary: The author told the model to go ahead as recommended: a sol review of the revised 143 and the generated SQL, then widening the generator's scope; he raised no objection to effectivity as one row per change (143 section 13 item 1).

Bundled the revised 143 with five generated files (staging, milestone, effectivity, status-tracking, hub) into scratch/REVIEW_143b.md and sent it to sol, framed against the standard, up to five findings.

sol reviewed the revised 143 and five generated files (the first call never started; the second answered) and failed them with five findings: a failed rebuild of a date that succeeded leaves rows; identical rows within one table collapse; late tied versions renumber; the source's closing time is not kept; an empty table writes undated status rows.

check.expected: generated SQL as the note says; deterministic, idempotent, append-only; exact reconstruction incl. zero-length and tied versions; nothing silently lost; a failed batch leaves nothing

summary: Applied findings 1, 2, 4 and 5: load_run on every row and nsdn_meta.dbt_invocations by project hooks, the pre-hook deleting rows of unsuccessful runs; only current-versus-history duplicates merged; source_closed_at in status tracking; the batch named by the runner's variable. Finding 3 stated as an assumption with a loud failure. Three checks added to the suite; all eight pass on the first scope.

Widened the generator to all 31 base tables: reading satellites, a satellite from another table than its hub's with a multi-table audit, the bridge's effectivity by presence with its surrogate and a link audit, and the country resolved in the same extract; fixed annotated valid times; staging made tables (491 s to 173 s for the first day). Staged the three complete extracts (cold-room history split in 20 MB parts, all checksums matching).
Ran the cloud suite on the full scope (216 tables, 777 tests per load) over the three complete extracts: all eight checks pass; 5,360,224 delivered versions reconstruct exactly.

check.expected: the eight checks of test_load.py pass on the whole WWI raw vault
check.observed: all eight pass; 216 tables; 5,360,224 versions reconstructed

summary: Put generator 0.2.0 live (c8e4355; six stray test files removed in 4fd0d47) after setting the 0.1.0 warehouse aside; the runner replayed 2016-05-31 to 06-02, all ok (522, 893, 905 s); the published vault equals the cloud clean load in all 216 tables, 17,346,219 rows.

check.expected: the runner's full-scope load on the author's machine equals the cloud suite's clean load
check.observed: 216 of 216 tables identical in count and content fingerprint (load_run excluded)

summary: The author agreed with the recommendations: the bridge's audit satellite on the link and staging as tables (143 section 13 items 12 and 14), and advancing the simulation so the vault loads new data.
verbatim: agree with your recommendations. Please proceed.

summary: Recorded the agreement (26987f8) and requested the sandbox job to advance two simulated days (s12-advance-204545), 2016-06-03 and 06-04, each with a full extract.

The job simulated 2016-06-03 (Friday, 100 new orders) and 06-04 (Saturday, 53); the runner loaded both, ok with 777 tests passing, in 1,330 and 1,324 s; the same extracts loaded in the cloud in 317 and 330 s; the five-day vaults are identical in all 216 tables (17,457,746 rows).

check.expected: new simulated days load with all tests passing and equal on both machines
check.observed: both ok; 216 of 216 tables identical; new orders 100 and 53 as the simulator reported

summary: Found that one test, late arrivals on the cold-room audit, took 191 of 305 s per load (a comparison of every reading with every other); rewrote it to compare with the latest earlier version only (generator 0.2.1): same answers on the constructed late arrival and on 2016-06-04, 2 s.

Put 0.2.1 live (4bee3cf); the runner's rebuild of 2016-06-04 passed in 572 s (previous rebuild 1,198 s). The rest is mostly the cold-room history re-read every load (staging 69 s, nothing-dropped 74 s, audit completeness 36 s).

check.expected: a daily load well under the 15 to 22 minutes seen
check.observed: 572 s for a rebuild of one day on the author's machine

notes: A conversation separate from the one that ran S12-001 to S12-027, on a different model; S12 was still open, so the steps are logged here.

summary: Read the entry, concept and process documents, the ADR index, handover 12, parts of the register, the generator and sandbox code and samples of the analysis record; ran check_repo.py and generate.py --check on a copy (both clean); gave the author 19 numbered points: 5 strengths, 10 concerns and 4 suggested next steps.
notes: The load suite and the PostgreSQL catalogue test were not run. HEAD was 21d47cf, 20 commits ahead of origin/main.

summary: Filed the assessment as a dated research note with its limits stated and its points linked to the rows they touch, pointed to it from PRC-OP-1, added the model to the vocabulary and to S12, and logged S12-028 to S12-031.
notes: Chosen without asking: a note under 30_research/notes rather than an XREV, because 510 asks one object per pass and forbids general assessment; PRC-OP-1 because it is the row for external review of the repository. No row opened, none changed in state.
